title: LibD: Scalable and Precise Third-party Library Detection in Android Markets
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
detection_method: Homogeny graph using Inclusion, Inheritance, and Call relations to recover library boundaries from bytecode; feature hashing via CFG opcode per basic block → method hash → class hash → instance fingerprint
module_decoupling: Homogeny graph — builds graph of class relations (inclusion, inheritance, call edges) and partitions it to recover library boundaries without relying on package names
matching_algorithm: Instance fingerprint matching via hierarchical hash chain (block → method → class → instance); clustering-based detection requires library to appear in ≥10 apps
obfuscation_handling: Opcode hashing inherently resilient to name-based obfuscation; homogeny graph handles package structure mutations since it uses structural relations not package names
r8_resilience: Not explicitly tested (pre-R8 era; tested on ProGuard-obfuscated apps)
lib_level_f1: Not explicitly reported as F1 — detected 1,954 libraries vs LibRadar's 670 on 1.4M apps
precision: False positive rate 25% vs LibRadar's 60.6% (precision inversely inferred ~75%)
recall: Higher than LibRadar (found 1,954 vs 670 libraries); absolute recall not computable without ground truth for 1.4M apps
speed: Scalable to 1.4M apps (specific per-app timing not reported)
partial_lib_handling: None — library must appear in ≥10 apps (binary threshold), no partial score
sbom_output: No — outputs library name list only, no version info, no standard format
open_source: No — reproducibility limited; no public repository found
transitive_deps: No — does not model dependency chains between libraries
strengths: Massive scale — evaluated on 1.4M apps across 10 markets
Homogeny graph recovers library boundaries without relying on package names (structural approach)
Opcode hashing inherently resilient to name-based obfuscation
Lower false positive rate (25%) than LibRadar (60.6%)
Ghost call detection — discovers calls to nonexistent functions revealing hidden behavior
Found google/gson had 421 packaging variations, demonstrating scale of packaging diversity
weaknesses: No version-level detection — clustering only, cannot distinguish library versions
Threshold requirement (≥10 apps) misses rare or app-specific libraries
impact_on_project: Demonstrates that opcode-based hashing and structural dependency graphs (not package names) are the right direction for obfuscation-resilient library detection. The homogeny graph concept for module decoupling is a precursor to CDG-based approaches and validates that structural relations survive obfuscation better than naming conventions. The ghost call detection technique is valuable for uncovering hidden/dependency behavior. However, the lack of version-level detection means LibD alone is insufficient for SBOM generation — version identification must be added. The 421 packaging variations of gson highlight the scale of the version-identification challenge.
